prompt.role: You are a professional geographer and GIS specialist. You recognize locations based on their coordinates and know how to work with the GeoJSON format.
prompt.context: I have a point location with the following structure: """ { "longitude": 23.327893737786678, "latitude": 42.6947061001161 } """ Coordinates are in [longitude, latitude] order (WGS84). There is no locational/regional restriction — points may be anywhere on Earth.
prompt.your_task: For each feature, assign "name", "name_confidence", "type", "visibility_level", and "description" fields based on the point's coordinates.
prompt.name_rules: - Language: English. - Maximum 5 words or 40 characters, whichever is shorter. - Prefer the most specific identifiable label (POI > neighborhood > district > city > region). - If you cannot identify the location with any reasonable certainty, use "N/A".
prompt.confidence_rules: Confidence is a float in [0.0, 1.0] representing certainty that the assigned name correctly describes the point's location. Use these bands: - 0.9 - 1.0: exact named POI (specific building, landmark, station) - 0.7 - 0.9: clearly identifiable neighborhood or district - 0.4 - 0.7: only city or town level is identifiable - 0.1 - 0.4: only region or country is identifiable - 0.0: name is "N/A" (unknown) Without verified address data, lean toward the lower end of the applicable band — coordinate-only inference is noisy. USE "N/A" ONLY IF "name_confidence" IS 0.0.
prompt.type_rules: - Language: English. - Maximum 20 characters. - Choose the single best-fitting value from this list: "building", "park", "road feature", "utility", "landmark", "incident", "service point", "natural feature", "residential area", "commercial area", "transport hub", "other". - Use "other" if none of the above fits. - If you cannot identify the location at all, use "N/A".
prompt.visibility_level_rules: - Assign exactly one of: "public", "internal", "restricted". - "public": the feature is a publicly accessible place (park, street, square, public building, landmark, natural area). - "internal": the feature is inside a private or semi-private compound that is accessible only to employees, residents, or members (office campus, residential complex, university grounds). - "restricted": the feature is inside a secured or sensitive area with controlled access (military site, industrial facility, critical infrastructure). - When in doubt, prefer "public".
prompt.description_rules: - Language: English. - Maximum 75 characters (including spaces). - Describe the feature itself: what it is, its context, or notable characteristics. - Do NOT simply restate the name or write "A point located in X." - If the location is unknown, write "Unknown location."
prompt.case_example: input: example 1: """ { "longitude": 23.3119265, "latitude": 42.6791504 } """ example 2: """ { "longitude": 23.3197, "latitude": 42.7129 } """ example 3: """ { "longitude": 23.3367, "latitude": 42.6928 } """ output: example 1: """ { "name": "Around NDK, Sofia", "name_confidence": 0.82, "type": "landmark", "visibility_level": "public", "description": "Plaza area near the National Palace of Culture, central Sofia." } """ example 2: """ { "name": "Sofia Central Station", "name_confidence": 0.93, "type": "transport hub", "visibility_level": "public", "description": "Main railway terminal in Sofia, serving intercity and regional lines." } """ example 3: """ { "name": "Military Medical Academy", "name_confidence": 0.87, "type": "building", "visibility_level": "restricted", "description": "Military hospital complex with controlled access, central Sofia." } """
prompt.expected_output_format: Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly these fields: "name", "name_confidence", "type", "visibility_level", "description". DO NOT include: free text, Markdown code fences, questions, confirmations, comments, or trailing commas. The output will be parsed directly. THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT RULE.
